scores.evidence: Discovery → Foundations → Golden-path CI → CD → Pilot in prod → Migration waves
scores.rationale: Phases run substrate (runners, registry, identity, GitOps) upward to templates, CD, gates, migration, with a done-when proof per early phase.

scores.evidence: a "hello world" service can be built, pushed and deployed to dev entirely through the platform
scores.rationale: A thin end-to-end slice exists in Phase 1 but only to dev; Phase 0 is discovery and prod arrives around week 12–16.

scores.evidence: decisions are written up as ADRs (architecture decision records)
scores.rationale: Irreversible decisions are listed with some recommended defaults, but there are no flip conditions or revisit triggers.

scores.evidence: Grouped by archetype... Complex ~7: Legacy, stateful, unusual tooling, or the most critical services
scores.rationale: Shared foundations and versioned templates precede leaf services, but the plan does not order by blast radius within phases, and critical services go last by risk rather than breadth.

scores.evidence: OIDC from CI to the cloud (no long-lived keys) and a secrets manager
scores.rationale: Security appears in Phase 1 (identity), Phase 2 (SCA, signing) and Phase 4, but Phases 0, 3, 5 and 6 have little, and the main gates come late.
DORA baseline is in Phase 0 and the diagram says to start early, but there's no concrete observability work in Phases 1–2, and dashboards arrive in Phase 6.

scores.evidence: Define the platform itself as code (Terraform, Pulumi or similar) from day one.
scores.rationale: IaC, versioned templates and GitOps give reproducibility, but it isn't treated explicitly in every phase, such as pinned builds or hermetic environments.

scores.evidence: Roll back automatically when SLOs or error rates breach thresholds.
scores.rationale: Resilience shows up in Phase 3 (rollback drill), Phase 5 (side-by-side runs) and Phase 6 (on-call), but not in Phases 1–2, such as runner or platform failure handling.
The plan never addresses whether an AI layer applies, so it earns no N/A credit.

scores.evidence: Building every feature before the pilot. Ship a thin version end to end first.
scores.rationale: Later items such as preview environments, the portal and complex services are placed in later phases, but there are no explicit pull-forward conditions.

note: A sound, well-ordered CI/CD plan with a strong pilot-then-migrate approach, but it lacks flip conditions, has no prod walking skeleton early, has thin observability and resilience in early phases, and never addresses the AI layer.
